edges.reason: The acacia_wall_sign is mounted on a jungle plank structure inside the jungle zone; player must locate the jungle area first to find and mine it
The nether corner entrance is adjacent to the jungle zone; player must explore the jungle area to discover the path to the netherrack section
After mining debris in the nether corner, player returns to the station area and accesses the material chest containing the damaged iron sword and iron ingots needed for anvil repair
Repairing the sword at the anvil places the player at the station area where the crafting table is 2 blocks away; player has already opened the material chest containing acacia planks
After anvil repair, player is at the station area and has already accessed the material chest (for iron ingots) which also contains the 9 coal needed for coal_block crafting
The consumable chest at ~1,0,-5 is directly behind the brewing stand at ~1,0,-3; interacting with the stand leads player to notice and open the adjacent chest containing the stew
Poisonous potato is in the same consumable chest behind the brewing stand; player discovers it after brewing stand interaction reveals the nearby chest
Suspicious stew applies Hunger II effect that drains the hunger bar below 20, which is mechanically REQUIRED for eating poisonous_potato (a normal food needing non-full hunger)
Crafting slabs requires opening the material chest which also contains 6 pumpkins; player discovers pumpkins during slab crafting, then locates the nearby farmer villager to trade

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The jungle zone is centered at [8,1,8] relative to spawn with jungle logs, leaves, podzol, and vines. max_distance=5 requires the player to actually walk ~6 blocks from spawn (which is ~11 blocks away from target). facing_tolerance=90 is generous since the jungle is a large area and the player just needs to be looking generally toward it.

Uses inventory_has because mining an acacia_wall_sign drops an acacia_sign item into the player's inventory. The sign is at ~9,2,6 facing south on the jungle plank wall. Player starts with no acacia_sign, so having one confirms successful mining. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks.

Uses inventory_has because mining ancient_debris with a diamond pickaxe drops the ancient_debris block as an item into inventory. The block is at ~-9,0,8 in the nether corner. Player has a diamond pickaxe (given via /give) and starts with no ancient_debris in inventory. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks.

Uses inventory_has because the damaged iron sword is stored in the material chest at ~-3,0,-5 (Slot 4), NOT in the player's starting inventory. The player must retrieve it from the chest and repair it at the anvil using iron ingots. Having an iron_sword in player inventory confirms retrieval from the chest, which combined with the dependency chain (player is at station area after mining) implies anvil repair as the natural action.

Uses inventory_has because crafting acacia slabs (3 acacia planks in a row → 6 slabs) results in acacia_slab items in the player's inventory. Player starts with no acacia_slab. min_count=1 for robustness in case player only picks up partial output from crafting table. This is the preferred rule type for craft tasks.

Uses inventory_has because crafting a coal block (9 coal in 3x3 grid → 1 coal_block) results in the coal_block item in the player's inventory. The chest provides exactly 9 coal. Player starts with no coal_block. This is the preferred rule type for craft tasks.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is an interaction task and no direct GUI-open event is available in the rule types. The brewing stand is at [1,0,-3]. max_distance=2 ensures the player is within right-click interaction range. facing_tolerance=45 ensures the player is looking directly at the stand, strongly implying intentional interaction rather than passing by. This is the best available proxy for GUI interaction.

Uses inventory_has(bowl) because in Java Edition, eating suspicious_stew returns a bowl to the player's inventory (same as mushroom_stew and rabbit_stew). The player starts with no bowl in inventory, and there is no other bowl source in the scene. Having a bowl is definitive proof of stew consumption.

Uses inventory_has because the player must pick up poisonous_potato from the consumable chest before eating it. The dependency chain ensures suspicious_stew is eaten first (applying Hunger II effect that drains the hunger bar below 20), which mechanically enables eating the poisonous_potato. Pickup from chest confirms the player has accessed the item and intends to consume it. This is an accepted limitation — pickup strongly implies consumption in a goal-directed agent context.

Uses inventory_has because selling 6 pumpkins to the farmer villager yields 1 emerald. The player starts with no emeralds, and there is absolutely no other emerald source in the scene. Having an emerald in inventory is definitive proof that the villager trade was completed successfully. This is the preferred rule type for trade/sell tasks.

scene_description: A compact multi-zone scene with four distinct areas within 15 blocks of spawn: (1) Jungle Zone (NE, ~5-12/~5-12) with jungle trees, podzol, vines, and an acacia wall sign on a jungle plank structure; (2) Nether Corner (NW, ~-12 to -6/~5-12) with netherrack walls/floor/ceiling, ancient debris, and a soul lantern entrance; (3) Station Area (center-south, ~-3 to 1/~-3 to -5) with crafting table, anvil, brewing stand, and two chests; (4) Trading Post (SW, ~-4 to -6/~-7 to -8) with a farmer villager, hay bale, composter, and barrel. Player spawns in survival mode with 30 XP levels and a diamond pickaxe.
task_text: Explore the jungle outpost: find the jungle area, mine the acacia wall sign, mine ancient debris in the nether corner with your diamond pickaxe, repair the iron sword at the anvil, craft acacia slabs and a coal block at the crafting table, interact with the brewing stand, eat the suspicious stew then the poisonous potato, and sell pumpkins to the farmer villager.
design_notes:
FINAL VERSION — All critical issues resolved through team iteration:

1. /gamemode survival @p — ensures mining, eating, crafting work correctly
2. /xp set @p 30 levels — provides XP for anvil repair cost
3. Iron sword in chest Slot 4 (not /give) — makes inventory_has milestone non-trivial
4. Diamond pickaxe via /give — needed immediately for ancient debris mining
5. Suspicious stew with Hunger II (EffectAmplifier:1) for 300 ticks (15 sec) — reliably drains hunger bar below 20 to enable poisonous_potato consumption
6. Nether corner entrance gap at ~-7,0-2,5 — ensures player can walk in
7. Acacia wall sign at ~9,2,6 facing south — visible when approaching from spawn direction
8. All zones within 15 blocks of spawn — compact and fully reachable
9. Exactly 6 pumpkins matching villager trade requirement
10. 2 poisonous potatoes (buffer for failed eat attempts at full hunger before stew effect kicks in)

SPATIAL LAYOUT:
- Spawn: 0,0,0 (player faces south by default)
- Jungle Zone: NE quadrant (~5-12 x, ~5-12 z)
- Nether Corner: NW quadrant (~-12 to -6 x, ~5-12 z)
- Station Area: Center-south (~-3 to 1 x, ~-3 to -5 z)
- Trading Post: SW (~-4 to -6 x, ~-7 to -8 z)
- Decorative jungle log: Near spawn at ~3,0,-2 (visual cue toward jungle)
